summary.name: Netty
summary.one_liner: Netty is a free, open-source macOS menu bar dot that shows whether the internet really answers, with latency, jitter, packet loss and speed tests.
use_cases: Check whether the internet is really reachable when Wi-Fi shows connected
Spot a poor connection that causes lagging calls or stalled pages
Run a speed test from the menu bar on a schedule
Get notified when the connection drops and returns
See the Wi-Fi name, VPN status and local or public IP at a glance
summary.what_it_does: Netty shows a colored dot in the macOS menu bar: green when online, yellow when latency, jitter or packet loss is high, and red when there is no internet. It checks every 10 seconds by asking Apple's captive portal page and Google's, and by timing a handshake with 1.1.1.1. Clicking the icon triggers an immediate check. A speed test uses Apple's built-in networkQuality to measure download, upload and responsiveness, run on demand or on a schedule. The popover shows Wi-Fi name, VPN status, and local and public IP addresses, and the user can customize sections, icon style, click actions and the color thresholds.
notable: Checks the internet itself, not just Wi-Fi association, and flags captive portals such as hotel sign-in pages as offline
Uses Apple's built-in networkQuality for speed tests, with no extra test servers
No analytics, telemetry or account; only the check requests leave the Mac
Distributed via GitHub and Homebrew rather than the Mac App Store
caveats: Not notarized by Apple yet, so the first launch needs manual approval in System Settings, Privacy & Security
Wi-Fi network name requires Location permission; without it, only 'Wi-Fi' is shown
Scheduled speed tests skip an iPhone hotspot
